question.text: In a 'Parallel Structure' for an India-focused AIF, the offshore fund in Singapore and the onshore AIF in India both:

answer.text: Invest directly into Indian investee companies side-by-side, with the offshore fund making independent investment decisions.
Pool offshore and domestic capital into a single Indian master fund.
Invest only outside India to avoid SEBI regulation.
Must be managed by the same investment manager as a single legal entity.

explanation.text: The Logic: XIX-D pp. 104-109 describes a parallel structure in which the offshore fund invests directly in Indian investee companies alongside the domestic AIF, instead of investing into a master fund, and the offshore fund makes independent investment decisions per its own mandate. The Trap: Single-master pooling describes a unified/feeder structure rather than a parallel structure. "Invest only outside India" is false. The single-manager / single-entity claim contradicts the parallel nature of the two vehicles. Note: The pages checked do not specify that each vehicle has its own independent investment committee or that offshore LPs hold a deal-level veto. The POEM consideration is tied only to the source-backed cautious, non-binding advisory relationship between the offshore vehicle and any Indian adviser.
